Issue one immutable current-authority authority Ack for a fully signed Control Move. Local device/Agent authorities use the same typed request and outcome without an HTTP hop. A caller canonically sorts distinct authority Acks and may submit the resulting receipt set only when the current notary profile quorum and common-window rules are satisfied.

Authenticated submission of one complete signed_defer or signed_reject. The receiver loads the durable accepted proposal and its immutable canonical ControlProposalAck, recomputes proposal_ack_digest, verifies the exact Realm/proposal/authority-set/deadline/defer chain and quorum, then atomically persists the decision. Exact decision replay is byte-identical duplicate; conflicting terminal or post-Seal decisions fail closed. For ak.device.revoke, only a valid signed_reject for the exact proposal/Ack (therefore the exact reducer-derived device and generation) clears that proposal's revocation_pending record; it clears no other pending revoke for the device.

Authenticated exact proposal observation surface. Returns only the durable authority discriminator, canonical Ack when applicable, verified decision chain and covering Seal state for the requested Realm/proposal digest. control_proposal_ack permits the closed pending/deferred/overdue/rejected/sealed chain and always carries Ack; the narrow ackless_event_proof branch permits only pending/sealed and carries no Ack, decision or Ack-derived deadline fault. ak.device.revoke is always control_proposal_ack. The operation cannot mint an Ack, synthesize a reject or mutate pending state; unauthorized and unknown selectors are non-enumerating.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned device_message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates. An encrypted DC has one immutable scope-derived MLS group and monotonic epoch lineage; the response carries exact current group_state_ref+digest. Repair is an ordinary Commit in that group. If all private group state is lost, the old DC Realm is terminal and a new conversation requires a new Realm id. No second group, epoch reset or timeout takeover exists.

Initial durable Event publication uses EventInitialSubmission: the signed Event remains the only business fact, while AuthorizationLease and optional CbaProofBundle values are independently verified publication evidence outside the Event digest. Before accepting a device-authored Event or appending principal_server_admission, the origin Principal Server reads the exact durable device revocation state in the same admission transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and zero Event/proof writes. Accepted ak.device.revoke is Ack-required and atomically writes its derived exact device/generation pending record. For a locally authored Realm Event, canonical acceptance, the complete distinct recipient-service target set and every target outbox intent commit atomically. A missing route creates durable pending_route and never rejects the Event; each send rechecks the frozen exact member/delivery-binding authority, authority loss terminally cancels the old target, and submit exposes only pending_delivery_count; clients derive delivery state as pending iff the count is non-zero. The ingress MUST persist and return the original IngressReceipt before lease expiry; byte-identical retry returns the stored receipt without changing received_at. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer remains the authoritative state machine and re-checks token commitment, allowlist, replay, proposal and expiry state. The direct_conversation_founding branch remains its closed four-Event atomic unit: Realm create, peer membership join, main Strand create and founder membership join. The agent_membership_cascade branch is the only controller-cascade carrier: atomic_self_leave accepts the controller terminal Event and the exact pre-state Agent leave set all-or-nothing; emergency_terminal accepts a third-party terminal Event and atomically freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent without synthesizing Agent Events; emergency_cleanup accepts only the same initiator's complete signed Agent leave set and commits it atomically. Effective Agent membership is invalid immediately after the terminal transition, independent of cleanup completion. Exact replay returns the original byte-identical outcome, while the same cleanup intent with different canonical content is duplicate_conflict.

PCR-only pre-sign preparation for one exact prospective successor Seal. The receiver requires the exact current predecessor frontier and exact accepted uncovered Control Event set, derives the sole eligible holder from the accepted PCR genesis ak.realm.create principal_server_id after validating its principal_server_admission and historical signer evidence, chooses sealed_at, issues and durably stores every required AvailabilityReceipt plus authenticated holder-signer evidence, and returns every-and-only dependency with canonical digests. It fails closed when the local Principal Server is not that create-locked holder, the default min_holders=1 contract cannot be met, or any requested basis is stale or incomplete. The response is preparation material only and does not commit a Seal.

Submit one client-signed Seal directly. A Seal is not an Event and never uses EventInitialSubmission. Except for the canonical genesis exception, the signature MUST satisfy predecessor governance notary actor/threshold rules. The receiver recomputes Seal id, recursive coverage, completeness_root, state_root, signer authority and signature.

Return the complete durable frozen fanout target set for one caller-visible accepted Event. Unknown and invisible Events share not_found. Rows use stable opaque target_id and are sorted byte-wise; service_id is included only when the caller can currently read an exact contributing member delivery-binding. The query has no retry, route-resolution or delivery side effect.
Actor/data Event causal frontier only. actor_id is required; Realm Seal discovery is exclusively ak.self.seals.read.frontier.v1.
Realm Seal frontier discovery. Returns the complete canonical accepted Seal antichain, governance health and observation coordinate.

Exact Seal-only resolve by seal_refs. Event selectors are forbidden. Optional self history_traversal_access names one retained request receipt/archive replica basis digest and authorizes only Seal refs in its exact target-to-base traversal cut; unknown and unauthorized remain indistinguishable.

Near-current stateless group_security_frontier query only. The caller binds exact proof_base_basis and proof_target_basis antichains plus the closed frontier selector. Bulk or old history uses receipt-bound direct accepted-Seal traversal through standard Event/Seal/dependency resolve.

Resolve a caller-split batch of exactly three content-addressed evidence kinds: AvailabilityReceipt, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence, and MinimalMetadataMlsLeafSignerEvidence. Optional self history_traversal_access is the sole retained-cut visibility exception. The operation is cursor-free and returns no partial result when the complete same-shape outcome exceeds byte_limit or 8 MiB.

Dereference exact event_id/event_digest selectors. Optional self history_traversal_access authorizes only delta Control Moves in one retained target-to-base direct traversal cut and is mutually exclusive with ordinary timeline visibility. Point lookup is not a range scan and never attaches covering/first-activation Seals; Control-Move effectiveness uses Seal frontier/resolve.
Canonical safe and idempotent Events range scan. HTTP uses RFC 10008 QUERY with typed JSON content.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Authorized account-internal resolution audit evidence: PCR realm id, genesis Event and receipt, current and bounded predecessor resolution Events, and an accepted Seal covering the disclosed state. Authorization is only a current holder session bound to the exact principal_authority pair; recovery first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes the current holder rather than introducing a second audit authorization path. Unknown account, wrong authority pair and unauthorized caller share one anti-enumeration outcome. history_depth is the closed range 0..256 with default 0 and MUST NOT be silently capped; after_resolution_event_ref stops the disclosed segment exclusively at a known ancestor in this account's lineage and requires history_depth >= 1. A truncated segment sets history_complete=false and returns next_audit_cursor; omitted history is unknown, never absent.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. subject_id and recipient_id are server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Transaction-bound monotonic erasure of the exact old secret_storage and mls_history series reserved by a SecurityRotationTransaction. Partial outcomes persist per series/object; exact retry never resurrects or rewrites an erased item. A complete outcome carries the sole canonical erase confirmation.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the stored terminal outcome, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Session-authenticated entry to the canonical KeyPackage claim carrier. The participant supplies the same closed device|native_agent requester_authorization and stable service_binding with source/destination service DIDs used by peer claim; deployment trust domains are absent from participant-authored bytes and are bound only by the Principal Server's verified resolution plus outer RFC 9421 headers. The local Principal Server verifies the current durable requester authorization and exact current membership delivery binding; local source=destination uses the same destination-authority CAS, while remote targets are durably relayed without rewriting the participant-signed body. Uncertain outcomes are queried by the original claim_request_id and request digest before any exact resend.

Carries exactly one direct-holder signed report_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned report fields. The Event kind is ak.self.moderation.report; this self endpoint accepts only absent/self provenance and forbids source_provider, delegated executor, Applet and MIMI-facade provenance. event.actor_id and payload.reporter must equal the authenticated session principal. There is no path Realm: event.realm_id, payload.realm_id, signed scope_ref and the accepted target's derived governance scope must match exactly. Realm-default reports may omit payload.effective_scope; Circle reports must sign the exact Circle scope. The target must be accepted and visible to the reporter; absent, invisible and scope-mismatched targets use the same not_found response. This DataEvent carries seal_ref plus auth_context and cannot carry seal_basis or preconditions. The service forwards exact signed bytes through ordinary Event admission and never authors, rebuilds, co-signs, maps an operation ref to another target or adds a concurrency guard. report_id is derived by retyping the accepted Event id and the stored submit outcome has status=submitted. Exact replay returns that byte-identical outcome without a second log or queue append; the same Event identity with different bytes returns duplicate_conflict. routed_to is omitted for an ordinary reporter and may be returned only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the exact scope.

Authorization-gated data-plane observation returning the exact durable franking proof Event, its target Event, the first covering signed Seal, an RFC 6962 inclusion path against data_event_set_root, and historical service signer evidence. It never substitutes a control-plane delta proof.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_arkret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version and exact carrier support are discovered via *.describe / supported_operation_bundles (see sync/api-conventions.md).

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT mint the cursor id, choose updated_at, rebuild the payload or co-sign. Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Reads only the profile-private submit/read/review/cancel/invite-consume audit trail for one application. Applicant, eligible reviewer, or explicitly authorized Realm auditor only.
Candidate-profile private applicant cancellation. The caller and detached receipt signer must both be the original applicant.

Candidate-profile private reviewer decision. The reviewer-signed receipt binds the exact application revision and a capability grant/frontier proof; stale, expired or unauthorized decisions fail closed.

Candidate-profile private application intake. The applicant-signed receipt binds the accepted knock, policy/revision/private-body digests and applicant DID. The receipt and private body commit atomically and never enter shared Realm history.
Lists candidate application metadata. Reviewers and each matching applicant receive the protected body; other Realm members receive only application_pending placeholders.
Reads one candidate application for its applicant or an eligible reviewer. Every successful private-body read emits ak.audit.accessed.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Carries exactly one caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy EventInitialSubmission. The request contains moderation_policy_event and no unsigned policy projection; the closed Event payload contains only value, whose value is the complete policy object. event.realm_id must equal the path Realm, event.actor_id must equal the authenticated session actor, and the exact submitted bytes pass ordinary Event admission without service authorship, rebuilding, co-signing or precondition injection. The Event carries exactly one signed head_eq against ak:cell:ak.component.realm.moderation_policy.v1:null naming the complete settled value or null when absent. Admission follows the capability registry and accepts ak.realm.moderation_policy or ak.policy.manage; Realm ownership alone grants no write authority. Organization-approval constraints and any extra action capability required by policy contents are evaluated during admission. Exact byte replay of an accepted Event returns the byte-identical stored outcome; identity/body conflict, stale head, Bottom or multiple applicable CAS guards fails closed with zero additional writes.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Submits the caller-signed ak.realm.link Control Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. The edge is event.payload and the source Realm is event.realm_id, which MUST equal the path realm_id. General directed cycles are valid and traversal uses a visited set; admission rejects only self-reference, invalid kind, invalid payload, or an illegal FSM transition. Self-reference returns schema_violation with reason_code realm_link_self_reference; an illegal transition returns failed_precondition with reason_code realm_link_invalid_transition.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Submits the caller-signed tombstoning ak.realm.link Move (payload.status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. link_kind is named in the signed payload rather than a query parameter, because a query parameter is outside the bytes the caller signs; payload.target_realm_id MUST equal the path target_realm_id. Removing an edge is the same durable Event kind as creating one, so this operation keeps its event_log effect.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organization_ids hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hint_ids are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

After ak.policy.manage admission, a settled direct declaration is deleted by the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server Move with the exact payload {"tombstone":true} and head_eq for the complete declaration; the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it, which is why this DELETE carries a request body the way ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete.v1 already does. The registered cas_register effect sets that value in the per-Realm cell; effective reads then ignore the direct binding and resume governed_by fallback or local-only capability evaluation. Repeating DELETE against a settled tombstone is an idempotent empty success and MUST NOT change the cell or state_root. A never-written or inherited-only direct cell returns not_found and MUST NOT mutate an ancestor.
Reads the projected ak.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_organization_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Submits the caller-signed durable ak.realm.policy_server declaration Move (admission capability ak.policy.manage); the service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize it. The declaration is event.payload and the Realm is event.realm_id, which MUST equal the path realm_id. Reducer validates the DID, canonical HTTPS policy-check URL and on_timeout enum. When the direct cell already has a settled declaration or tombstone, the Move MUST carry head_eq for that complete value and the caller attaches it, because preconditions are inside the signed bytes; an absent direct cell is the only initial write.

Continues only the next step derived from the transaction kind and accepted-step prefix length. request_digest and prepared_plan_digest MUST equal the resource, while expected_accepted_step_count MUST equal the current prefix length; the endpoint is not a generic step or Saga executor. Client attestation is required only for issue_terminal_receipt or local_commit and must bind transaction/request/plan plus the pre-reserved output_ref. When all coordinator-owned steps are accepted but the device is offline, terminal_result remains absent; device-attestation readiness is a computed view of the canonical next step and no coordinator phase/state is serialized.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the prepared plan, accepted step prefix and optional terminal result; callers derive the next action from kind plus prefix length. It MUST NOT synthesize progress from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.

Encrypted-only Signal Extension send rail for ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. Exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. It MUST NOT persist the envelope as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Create one immutable scope-private history request. The operation envelope may be at most 1 MiB, while the inner HistoryKeyRequest itself is independently capped at 64 KiB canonical bytes. Before success the service verifies the caller-pinned bootstrap/current bases and complete durable target cut, atomically pins every Seal, delta Control Move and registered dependency through request expiry, freezes the exact direct traversal intent, durably stores request/receipt bytes, generates a 32-byte CSPRNG response capability and returns its byte-stable HPKE-sealed carrier. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical accepted outcome; different intent under the same request_id conflicts.

List immutable current-member-only requests for the exact Realm/Circle scope. realm_id is required; circle_id absence selects Realm scope. The RRK-holder branch returns only requests whose ranges intersect an archive sealed to the caller's exact historical key.

Durably enqueue one immutable manifest or independently sealed chunk. Manifest admission first resolves and replays the receipt-retained direct Seal/Event/dependency cut, derives current requester incarnation, join floor, winning MLS transitions and current monotone history_access, and atomically writes the all-ranges admission or nothing. A chunk requires that accepted admission, then enforces current T1 and writes the recipient record plus attestation. Premature/mismatched chunks are dependency_missing with zero pending state. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical small accepted HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt.

Capability-addressed sequence-ordered response-stream read. Authorization: Arkret-History-Capability carries the only external locator and authorization value; unknown, expired, garbage-collected and unauthorized capabilities are same-shape not_found. One merged stream contains normal records and signed lost descriptors; ack_token commits every ordered {sequence,kind,response_id,entry_digest} through the page high-water cursor.

Capability-protected contiguous high-water ack. Every covered sequence requires a durable installed, cryptographically_rejected, superseded_duplicate or signed service_record_lost disposition. Manifest installed means descriptor installation only; no reject/lost/manifest disposition completes epoch coverage.

Recipient-bound byte-paged archive list. Query and cursor bind scope/key tuple, accepted evidence Event, complete holder_trusted_basis, holder authority and last ordering tuple. Every row carries the exact holder-accepted archive_replica_digest plus archive-lifetime direct traversal retention for its singleton epoch. The holder MUST use that digest as the closed SelfHistoryTraversalAccess coordinate and may resolve every Control Move/Seal/dependency required by that replay, including membership/policy/control metadata; archive/traversal digests, unrelated DataEvents and generic timeline scan are forbidden substitutes. Unknown/unauthorized/tuple mismatch is same-shape not_found.

Private S2S fanout of one byte-identical request+receipt to a closed exact current member delivery-binding service or exact RRK holder service with intersecting archive tuple. Destination authorization, TTL and bytes are signed; no public Event/DeviceMessage.

Private S2S relay of the immutable source record plus SourceRelayAttestation from the source's authenticated current local Principal Server to request_receipt.release_id. Destination validates the relay service against current source delivery/authority binding and performs the only final T1/release linearization. The two-service cut is not globally atomic; v1 assumes honest services and bounded TTL observation.

Near-current S2S group_security_frontier query only. It binds exact base/target Seal antichains and the closed selector; bulk or old history uses receipt/replica-bound direct Seal traversal through standard Event, Seal and governance-dependency resolve.

Authenticated S2S exact resolve of exactly three content-addressed evidence kinds: AvailabilityReceipt, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence, and MinimalMetadataMlsLeafSignerEvidence. Omitted history_traversal_access uses ordinary Realm/federation visibility; the optional pending_archive_replica branch is the sole retained-cut exception. Member request replicas never authorize traversal. Unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing selectors are same-shape; complete bounds failure returns no partial items or cursor.

Private immutable RRK archive replica to exact holder_id. It binds exact archive bytes, container Event, accepted evidence Event, complete holder_trusted_basis and archive-lifetime direct traversal retention for one epoch. First durable acceptance assigns one archive_sequence per semantic key; changing replicated_at cannot add a row. Exact duplicate returns the first byte-identical accepted receipt. Archive and replay closure are retained for the Realm recovery-material lifetime; v1 defines no remote GC/renewal.
